children: In Taiwan, unions at Micron Technology Inc. (MU, Financials) are seeking a bigger share of profits and heftier bonuses, threatening possible labor disruption.
Local media reports quoted by Seeking Alpha say the unions represent over 10,000 employees. Timing is everything for investors.
Execution and supply reliability are particularly critical as Micron enjoys robust demand for memory attached to AI infrastructure.
A strike in Taiwan could also create an operational risk when consumers are focused on securing enhanced memory capacity. The dispute also shows another result of the memory upcycle.
With profits rebounding, staff are demanding a bigger slice of the spoils through incentives and profit-sharing schemes.
Micron is in direct competition with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix in memory markets, so any disruption affecting production or deliveries could matter if rivals can absorb more demand.
There is so far no sign of an imminent strike and talks could yet settle the matter before it has any impact on operations.
Investors will now be watching to see if Micron can negotiate a deal with workers to avert any disruption to its Taiwan operations.

title: Micron's AI Memory Boom Just Ran Into a Labor Risk
